transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-01
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dana Kim (CTO - Mythos), Rajiv Menon (Lead ML Eng - Mythos), Hannah Lee (SRE - Mythos), Tom Alvarez (Product - Mythos)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be imperfect):
Redwood walked Mythos through the self-serve onramp path: sign-up, free credits, SDKs, and what hosted vs private pathways look like. Mythos clarified data privacy needs, expected load pattern (burst/steady), and internal timeline for a pilot. Action items were assigned for security artifacts and a perf baseline run.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. We're Samir from Redwood, AE, and with me is Elena, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dana: Good, thanks. Quick note I'm in SF timezone, just adjusting audio.
[00:12] Elena: Hi, Dana, hi Rajiv, Hannah, Tom. We'll keep this pretty practical, focus on time-to-first-token and your security questions.
[00:22] Rajiv: Thanks, yeah we've got a small team spinning up an assistant feature in our app and we want to get something end-to-end quickly but keep options open for private deployment later.
[00:30] Tom: We're particularly interested in cost — we have a lot of microcalls with varying prompt sizes.
[00:36] Samir: Perfect, that's exactly the scenario Redwood is often used for. Quick q: what's your current stack — do you have an existing LLM provider or are you starting fresh?
[00:45] Dana: Starting fresh, we've prototyped a couple models locally but nothing in prod. We want to evaluate Redwood hosted API first, probably use the free credits to run an integration sprint.
[00:54] Elena: Great — our PLG flow can get you to first call in under an hour typically. The free credits are usually enough for a week of smoke testing depending on token usage.
[01:05] Hannah: When you say "hosted", is data stored on Redwood's side? We have strict retention rules and need to KMS all things.
[01:12] Samir: Good callout — hosted means you call the Redwood public API; by default we retain logs short-term for diagnostics but for enterprise customers you can opt-out or use our private deployment. We also support customer-provided KMS in Private/Dedicated options.
[01:25] Rajiv: Can you give me a sense of the latency we'd see for typical gpt-style text gen? We need sub-200ms median for short responses.
[01:32] Elena: For small-ish models and short sequences we often hit single-digit token latency on dedicated pools, but hosted is more variable — medians in the 100-300ms range depending on sequence length and batching. Batching helps throughput but adds tail latency.
[01:45] Tom: So is that means if we go hosted and then later switch to VPC/on-prem we lose the work we've done?
[01:51] Samir: No, we try to make the API contract consistent. Model versions and rollout policies are separate from the infra. Migration requires some config for endpoints and network but prompts, SDK calls remain largely the same.
[02:03] Dana: What's the quickest path for us to evaluate? We want a clear time-to-first-token so engineering can plan.
[02:09] Elena: Self-serve sign-up, SDK quickstart, and we'll give you promo credits. Steps: register org, generate API key, run sample curl or SDK, you'll get a streaming response. If you want us to shadow the first integration we can do a 30-minute pairing session.
[02:24] [Speaker 1]: (murmur) the docs were good last time...
[02:28] Rajiv: What about request patterns — our app will have bursts (chatty sessions) with many small prompts. How does Redwood handle burstiness without blowing out cost?
[02:36] Elena: Two parts — batching and prefix/KV caching. For chat scenarios, KV cache makes repeated contexts cheap. For many concurrent short prompts, you can use reserved capacity (Dedicated) or set autoscale burst capacity. Also Optimize features suggest quantization and batching settings tuned to your load.
[02:52] Hannah: Can we get metrics at token level? We need token-level billing and logs per tx for auditing.
[02:58] Samir: Yes, Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model. For Private deployments we can push audit logs into your SIEM and tie them to your SAML identities.
[03:12] Dana: Security checklist — SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS, audit logs, data residency. Anything else we should think about?
[03:20] Elena: Network connection patterns matter: if you need VPC peering or a VPC connector we have docs. For on-prem we do an agent package. We also have contract terms for retention and deletion.
[03:31] Rajiv: On technical side: do you support multi-model routing in the API? We might want a small local model for cheap inference and a bigger model for complex prompts.
[03:39] Elena: Yes, model routing by policy is supported — we can route by latency or cost rules and fallback to a smaller quantized variant if bigger model is busy.
[03:48] Tom: Pricing — is self-serve per-token only? Or are there trial tiers?
[03:53] Samir: Hosted is usage-based (per token) for self-serve. We also issue free credits for new orgs to run the quickstart. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit. Private is enterprise licensing. We'll send a simple spreadsheet that lays unit economics for different throughput profiles.
[04:10] Dana: We'd like to run a perf baseline — sample payload sizes are 128-512 tokens, QPS target 5-25 on average with spikes to 100 for 30-60s.
[04:20] Rajiv: Also payloads include a few hundred KB of context occasionally (docs for retrieval). How does that affect costs?
[04:26] Elena: Retrieval context increases input tokens, so cost goes up linearly. For large context we recommend embeddings + retrieval to reduce prompt size. Also caching and chunking help. We'll follow up with a best-practices doc.
[04:40] Hannah: Any red flags on private deployment? We have auditors that expect HSM/KMS and air-gapped options.
[04:47] Samir: Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem packaging. Air-gapped involves a slightly longer onboarding (~4-6 weeks) and additional network validation.
[04:57] [00:05:00] Elena: Quick note: the PLG promo credits we give typically cover ~50k-200k tokens depending on the promotion; can adjust if you need more for heavier baseline tests.
[05:09] Rajiv: Great. For the perf baseline can we run both hosted and a small dedicated pool to compare latency/cost?
[05:16] Elena: Yes — we can provision a short-lived dedicated pool for a week (subject to capacity) or run a hosted baseline then show what Dedicated would look like for your QPS. We'll add both to the perf run plan.
[05:28] Tom: Any gotchas on SDKs? We mostly use Node and Python.
[05:32] Samir: SDKs for both languages, examples for streaming and function/tool calling. We also have a local dev docker image for integration tests.
[05:41] Dana: Timeline — we want a pilot within 2–3 weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[05:46] Samir: Yes — self-serve onramp can be same-day, pilot in 1–2 weeks with credits. Private/on-prem will push to 4–6+ weeks.
[05:55] Rajiv: Who are the internal stakeholders we should loop in? We'll bring Product, Infra/SRE, and Security.
[06:01] Samir: Sounds good. For the perf run we'll request a small set of sample prompts, payload sizes, and an API key for testing.
[06:07] [Speaker 2]: (crosstalk)
[06:09] Hannah: For auditability, does Redwood filter PII in logs by default?
[06:13] Elena: We don't redact by default; we can configure retention and redaction policies per customer. If PII filtering is required we can discuss transformers in the pipeline to mask sensitive fields before hitting the model.
[06:27] Dana: Ok, recap — Samir will send pricing + credits details, Elena sends security docs and perf run plan, Rajiv will supply sample payloads. Then we'll schedule a 60-min perf baseline next week.
[06:38] Samir: Yep. I'll send a calendar invite for the perf baseline after we nail down availability. Thanks everyone for the time.
[06:45] Tom: Appreciate it. Looking forward to the quickstart.
[06:48] Rajiv: Thanks, talk soon.
[06:50] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcription imperfections: occasional speaker labels use "Speaker 1/2" and some product names (K/V cache, KV-cache) were transcribed as "K V cash" or "K V cache" in parts. There may be minor mishearing of sequence lengths and timing.

References mentioned: "Quickstart guide link" (shared in chat), "SOC2 whitepaper" (to be sent), "perf spreadsheet" (price modeling doc).

End of transcript.
